html:
Pentucket was a Native village and band on the Merrimack River, where the city of Haverhill, Massachusetts, stands today. Its people spoke an Eastern Algonquian language and belonged to the Pennacook confederacy of the Merrimack valley.

They fished the river's runs of salmon and shad and farmed maize on its banks. Epidemics brought by European traders in the 1610s struck the peoples of the New England coast hard. In the early 1640s English settlers from the Massachusetts Bay Colony bought the land at Pentucket from local sachems and founded Haverhill. In the wars of the late 1600s many Pennacook moved north to join the Abenaki in New France.
